topic: angular acceleration from angular speed and time
statement: A turntable starts from rest and reaches an angular speed omega in a time interval t while rotating with constant angular acceleration. What is the magnitude of the turntable's angular acceleration?

omega.desc: final angular speed of the turntable

t.desc: time interval over which the turntable accelerates

topic: angular speed from linear speed and radius
statement: A point on the rim of a spinning wheel of radius r moves with a constant linear speed v. What is the magnitude of the wheel's angular velocity?

v.desc: linear speed of the point on the rim

topic: torque from a force applied at an angle
statement: A mechanic applies a force of magnitude F to a wrench at a distance r from the center of a bolt, at an angle theta relative to the line extending from the bolt through the point of application. What is the magnitude of the torque exerted on the bolt?

r.desc: distance from the bolt center to the point where the force is applied

theta.desc: angle between the force direction and the line from the bolt to the point of application

topic: rotational inertia of two point masses
statement: Two small beads of masses m_1 and m_2 are attached to a massless rigid rod at distances r_1 and r_2, respectively, from a fixed pivot axis perpendicular to the rod. What is the rotational inertia of the two-bead system about the pivot axis?

r_1.desc: distance of the first bead from the pivot axis

r_2.desc: distance of the second bead from the pivot axis

topic: rotational inertia of a uniform solid disk
statement: A uniform solid disk of mass m and radius R rotates about a fixed axis perpendicular to the disk and passing through its center. What is the rotational inertia of the disk about this axis?

m.desc: mass of the uniform solid disk

R.desc: radius of the uniform solid disk

topic: angular acceleration from net torque and rotational inertia
statement: A flywheel with rotational inertia I_wheel about its fixed axle experiences a constant net torque of magnitude tau. What is the magnitude of the angular acceleration of the flywheel?

tau.desc: magnitude of the net torque acting on the flywheel

I_wheel.desc: rotational inertia of the flywheel about its axle

topic: net torque from rotational inertia and angular acceleration
statement: A turbine rotor with rotational inertia I_turb about its spin axis undergoes an angular acceleration of magnitude alpha. What is the magnitude of the net torque acting on the rotor about its spin axis?

I_turb.desc: rotational inertia of the turbine rotor about its spin axis

alpha.desc: magnitude of the angular acceleration of the rotor

topic: inclined plane block coupled to a rotating pulley
statement: A block of mass m rests on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle theta with the horizontal, where the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is mu_k. A light, inextensible string attached to the block runs parallel to the incline up to a pulley of radius R and rotational inertia I_p mounted on a fixed, frictionless horizontal axle at the top of the incline. The string is wrapped around the pulley so that it unwinds without slipping relative to the pulley rim. The system is released from rest, and the block slides down the incline under gravitational acceleration g. Find the time required for the block to slide a distance d down the incline.

I_p.desc: rotational inertia of the pulley about its axle

theta.desc: angle of the inclined plane above the horizontal

mu_k.desc: coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline

d.desc: distance the block slides down the incline

topic: rotational inertia and uniform circular motion of a two-mass rod
statement: A light, rigid rod lies on a frictionless horizontal table and is pivoted at one end so it can rotate freely in the horizontal plane about a fixed vertical axis. Two small spheres of masses m_1 and m_2 are attached to the rod at distances r_1 and r_2 from the pivot, respectively. Starting from rest, a horizontal force of constant magnitude F is applied to the sphere of mass m_2 at a constant angle phi relative to the rod for a time interval t_0. At the end of time interval t_0, the applied force F is removed, and the rod continues to rotate at constant angular speed. Find the magnitude of the radial force exerted by the rod on the sphere of mass m_2 after the applied force is removed.

r_1.desc: distance from the pivot to m_1

r_2.desc: distance from the pivot to m_2

F.desc: magnitude of the applied horizontal force

phi.desc: angle between the applied force and the rod

t_0.desc: duration for which the force is applied

topic: rotational equilibrium of a pivoted rod held by a spring
statement: A light, rigid rod of length L is attached at one end to a frictionless horizontal pivot, with a small block of mass m attached to its free end. Under gravitational acceleration g, the rod is held stationary at an angle phi above the horizontal by a massless spring of spring constant k. One end of the spring is attached to the rod at a distance d from the pivot, and the spring exerts a force on the rod along a line making an angle theta with the rod to hold the system in rotational equilibrium. Find the elastic potential energy stored in the spring.

m.desc: mass of the block at the end of the rod

phi.desc: angle of the rod above the horizontal

d.desc: distance from the pivot to the spring attachment point

theta.desc: angle between the spring and the rod

topic: two-stage angular acceleration and braking of a flywheel
statement: A flywheel of radius R and rotational inertia I_w is mounted on a fixed, frictionless horizontal axle. Starting from rest, a constant tangential force of magnitude F is applied to the rim of the flywheel until the flywheel has rotated through an angle theta_1. At that instant, the tangential force F is removed, and a brake pad is pressed radially against the rim with a constant normal force of magnitude F_N. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the brake pad and the rim is mu_k. Find the total time from the start of the motion until the flywheel comes to rest.

I_w.desc: rotational inertia of the flywheel about its axle

F.desc: magnitude of the applied tangential force

theta_1.desc: angular displacement during the acceleration stage

F_N.desc: magnitude of the normal force exerted by the brake pad

mu_k.desc: coefficient of kinetic friction between the brake pad and the rim

topic: stepped pulley with two hanging blocks
statement: A stepped pulley consists of two rigidly joined coaxial drums of radii r_1 and r_2 and has total rotational inertia I_d about its fixed, frictionless horizontal axle. Two light, inextensible strings are wrapped in opposite senses around the two drums so that they unwind or wind without slipping relative to the drum rims. A block of mass m_1 hangs from the string on the drum of radius r_1, and a block of mass m_2 hangs from the string on the drum of radius r_2, with the masses and radii chosen so that m_2*r_2 exceeds m_1*r_1. The system is released from rest with both blocks at the same initial height under gravitational acceleration g. Find the vertical distance between the two blocks after a time interval t_0.

r_1.desc: radius of the drum attached to m_1

r_2.desc: radius of the drum attached to m_2

I_d.desc: rotational inertia of the stepped pulley about its axle

topic: Newton's second law for rotation and pivot reaction force
statement: A uniform rigid rod of mass M and length L is mounted on a horizontal frictionless pivot at one end, and its rotational inertia about the pivot is one-third of M times L squared. A small point object of mass m is rigidly attached to the rod at a distance d from the pivot (with d < L). In a uniform gravitational field of magnitude g, the rod is held horizontally and released from rest. Find the magnitude of the force exerted by the pivot on the rod immediately after release.

m.desc: mass of the attached point object

d.desc: distance of the attached object from the pivot

topic: Two-stage Atwood machine with a massive pulley
statement: A uniform disk pulley of mass M and radius R (whose rotational inertia about its fixed horizontal frictionless axle is one-half of M times R squared) has a light inextensible string passing over it without slipping. Blocks of masses m_1 and m_2 (with m_2 > m_1) hang vertically from the two ends of the string. Initially, the system is held at rest in uniform gravity with block m_1 resting on the horizontal floor and block m_2 at a height h above the floor, while the pulley is sufficiently high that neither block reaches it during the motion. The system is released from rest. When block m_2 hits the floor, it comes to rest immediately and remains on the floor, while block m_1 continues rising. Find the total angle through which the pulley rotates from the instant of release until block m_1 reaches its maximum height.

M.desc: mass of the uniform disk pulley

h.desc: initial height of block m_2 above the floor
